headline: Highest risk is broad-network Haystack paired with a non-runnable course artifact: no direct shared-channel pathway is documented, but MCP-enabled egress raises leakage and cascading-error concerns if wired together.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a non-runnable course repo with no I/O surfaces, while profile B can use MCP servers and REST APIs. A direct injection path is not documented, so the pair only becomes vulnerable if an operator manually bridges A’s content into B’s prompts or tools. That makes the blast radius small and configuration-dependent.
conditions: IF an operator copies content from agent_a outputs into agent_b prompts or MCP inputs
IF agent_b is configured to treat agent_a-produced text as instructions
mitigations: Keep agent_a and agent_b in separate workspaces
Disable copy-paste of untrusted text into agent_b tool prompts
Add a fixed instruction prefix that ignores embedded commands
Review any MCP tool schema before enabling it
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A exposes no data classes and has network egress none; agent B has broad egress and touches anonymous usage statistics. There is no shared filesystem or secret-bearing data shown, so leakage is limited unless an operator feeds sensitive material into B. The pair is not inherently a data-exfiltration setup from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF sensitive files are manually supplied to agent_b
IF agent_b is connected to external REST or MCP endpoints while processing user data
mitigations: Do not route sensitive files into agent_b
Restrict agent_b to approved endpoints only
Separate any local course materials from production data
Turn off telemetry if available
requires-engineering: enforce workspace and egress isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A has no declared write, network, or concurrency surfaces, while agent B can call REST APIs and MCP servers. Because A is not runnable and no shared mutable resource is documented, there is no default write-write conflict. Any conflict would require an external orchestrator to connect them to the same resource.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable external resource
IF an orchestrator grants agent_a write access not shown in its profile
mitigations: Assign separate resources to each agent
Avoid shared git or database targets
Run only one writer at a time
Document ownership of each API scope
requires-engineering: add locking around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent B is a search-RAG system with MCP and REST access, so if it consumes agent A’s outputs as retrieved facts, it may act on them without verification. Agent A is a course artifact, not a validated source, so the main risk is B amplifying incorrect or stale material into downstream actions. The pathway exists once the pair is wired together.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a output as authoritative retrieval context
IF agent_b triggers downstream actions based on unverified agent_a content
mitigations: Require citation checks before B acts
Insert a human review step for any action output
Mark agent_a content as untrusted by default
Limit B to read-only summarization
requires-engineering: add validation against source documents

E_compliance.rationale: Agent B touches anonymous usage statistics and has broad egress, while agent A shows no data classes touched and no egress. No residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to telemetry or accidental routing of sensitive inputs into B. A is not cited for a specific residency issue because none is present in the profile.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into agent_b
IF telemetry or external APIs receive data subject to residency or retention rules
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of agent_b
Review telemetry settings before use
Use a local-only deployment for sensitive workloads
Document retention for any logs
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data classes
